text: Chapter 1's finale — let's recap everything, and name the single idea underneath it.

Workspace and OneLake gave us the same container idea, with automatic shared storage. Lakehouse and warehouse gave us the same Delta format, two engines, chosen by who's actually querying. Notebooks and pipelines gave us the same PySpark, the same activity model. And capacities, Git, and monitoring gave us the operational layer, Fabric's own way.

Trace one real trip through it: a CSV, moved by a copy activity into a lakehouse's files, loaded into a real Delta table, cleaned by a notebook running real PySpark, related and summarized by a semantic model, and finally read by Power BI in Direct Lake mode — fast, current, with no copy ever made.

Every single stage there is something already covered — just now in Fabric's own UI. Same foundation, new platform. Chapter 1 complete. Next: real-time data engineering, where Fabric genuinely does something new.
